failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Query at hop 2: 'Who was the head coach of the Rhode Island Rams men's basketball team in 2012–13, and what is his relationship to the Arizona State men's basketball team head coach?' — This is a natural-language yes/no question format rather than a well-formed entity-targeted query.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 1 retrieved 'Bobby Hurley' and '2012–13 Rhode Island Rams men's basketball team' passages. Hop 2 query asks 'Who was the head coach of the Rhode Island Rams men's basketball team in 2012–13, and what is his relationship to the Arizona State men's basketball team head coach?' which retrieves nearly identical documents (same 'Bobby Hurley' and '2012–13 Rhode Island Rams' passages). Hop 3 query 'Dan Hurley, Robert Matthew Hurley, 2012-13 Rhode Island Rams basketball, Arizona State men's basketball' again retrieves the same core documents ('Bobby Hurley', '2012–13 Rhode Island Rams'). All three hops returned substantially the same information.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Passage_Content_Misreading
failure_modes.evidence: In the Bobby Hurley passage, it states Bobby 'was an associate head coach for Rhode Island on the staffs of his younger brother Dan.' This establishes Bobby is the OLDER brother (Dan is younger). The claim states 'The first year head coach...is the brother of Robert Matthew Hurley' which is technically correct but the solver summaries call Dan the 'younger brother' of Bobby, confirming the relationship direction. However, the claim's phrase 'head coach of Arizona State's highest ranked men's basketball team' is problematic: the passages describe Bobby as head coach of 'the Arizona State men's team' not 'Arizona State's highest ranked men's basketball team.' There is no evidence Arizona State has multiple men's basketball teams or ranking information to support this phrasing.
